answer_text:
We only need to determine the integer part of each term, not the exact value of \(a_n\).

First compute

\[
a_2=1+\frac1{a_1}+\ln a_1=1+1+0=2.
\]

We will prove that for every \(n\ge 2\),

\[
2\le a_n<3.
\]

Then \([a_n]=2\) for all \(n\ge 2\), while \([a_1]=[1]=1\).

---

### 1. Two useful logarithm bounds

For \(1\le t\le 2\), we have \(\frac1t>\frac12\), so

\[
\ln 2=\int_1^2 \frac{dt}{t}>\int_1^2 \frac{dt}{2}=\frac12.
\]

Also,

\[
\ln 3=\int_1^2 \frac{dt}{t}+\int_2^3 \frac{dt}{t}.
\]

Since \(\frac1t<1\) on \((1,2]\) and \(\frac1t\le \frac12\) on \([2,3]\),

\[
\ln 3<\int_1^2 1\,dt+\int_2^3 \frac12\,dt
=1+\frac12=\frac32.
\]

Thus

\[
\ln 2>\frac12,\qquad \ln 3<\frac32.
\]

---

### 2. Induction bound for \(a_n\)

Base case: \(a_2=2\), so \(2\le a_2<3\).

Assume for some \(n\ge 2\) that

\[
2\le a_n<3.
\]

Then

\[
\frac13<\frac1{a_n}\le \frac12
\]

and, since \(\ln x\) is increasing,

\[
\ln 2\le \ln a_n<\ln 3.
\]

Using the bounds above,

\[
a_{n+1}=1+\frac1{a_n}+\ln a_n
>1+\frac13+\frac12
=\frac{11}{6}>2,
\]

and

\[
a_{n+1}=1+\frac1{a_n}+\ln a_n
<1+\frac12+\frac32
=3.
\]

So

\[
2<a_{n+1}<3.
\]

Therefore, by induction,

\[
2\le a_n<3 \qquad \text{for all } n\ge 2.
\]

Hence

\[
[a_n]=2 \qquad \text{for all } n\ge 2.
\]

---

### 3. Compute \(S_n\)

Since \([a_1]=1\) and \([a_k]=2\) for \(k\ge 2\),

\[
S_n=[a_1]+[a_2]+\cdots+[a_n]
=1+2(n-1)=2n-1.
\]

\[
\boxed{2n-1}
\]
